results.title: Multiphoton Microscopy in the Biomedical Sciences XXVI
results.content: Multiphoton excitation optical microscopy intrinsically allows multimodal fluorescence imaging allowing 3D, super resolved and life-time imaging including image scanning microscopy. We will review the state-of-the-art multiphoton microscopes for in vivo imaging of living tissues and animal models, and describe a number of directions for continued development, including new laser sources, new spectral windows and optimum illumination schemes. Femtosecond lasers continue to drive advances in multiphoton imaging, enabling high-resolution visualization across a range of biological applications—from deep-tissue microscopy to label-free chemical contrast in cancer diagnostics. Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) discerns biomolecular states, interactions, and environments, by discriminating multiple probe lifetimes. We present next steps in EO-FLIM technology development and optimized optical designs for wide-field, high speed, and multiplexed lifetime imaging applications. In vivo optical metabolic imaging of human skin exposed to high altitude with an 80 MHz femtosecond fiber laser multi- photon FLIM tomograph (Invited Paper). The system enables high-resolution metabolic imaging by capturing fluorescence lifetimes of endogenous coenzymes NAD(P)H and FAD, revealing metabolic differences between healthy and cancerous tissues.
